title: CoDi: Subject-Consistent and Pose-Diverse Text-to-Image Generation
claim: Existing methods gain subject consistency by sacrificing pose diversity; ours breaks this trade-off, matching baseline diversity while achieving the highest consistency.
layout: 3 panels: two image grids (4 method rows x 3 prompts each) on left, scatter plot with trade-off band on right; captions beneath
description: The left two-thirds shows two image grids, (a) a barista sketch and (b) a porcelain princess figurine. Each grid has four rows labeled Vanilla SDXL, ConsiStory, StoryDiffusion and CoDi (ours), and three columns with italic prompt phrases on top. Baseline rows show repeated poses, such as the same stance at the espresso machine. The Vanilla SDXL and CoDi rows show varied poses. A dashed gray line separates the grids. The right panel (c) is a scatter plot of Subject Consistency (DINO-v2) on the x-axis against Pose Diversity on the y-axis. A light cyan diagonal band holds the baselines, running from Vanilla SDXL at top-left to StoryDiffusion at bottom-right. CoDi appears as a purple star in the top-right corner, with a pink 'Upper Right Better' arrow. Bold labels highlight CoDi.
caption: Comparison of subject-consistent generation methods: Vanilla SDXL [ref], ConsiStory [ref], StoryDiffusion [ref] and \ours (ours). (a&b) Existing methods sacrifice pose diversity for subject consistency, \eg, ConsiStory produces similar poses in Figure [ref] (a); and the lower right with hands placed in front in Figure [ref] (b). In contrast, \ours generates consistent subjects, while matching the pose diversity of Vanilla SDXL. (c) Subject consistency vs. pose diversity. Current methods struggle to balance the two, whereas \ours achieves both effectively.
abstract: Subject-consistent generation (SCG)-aiming to maintain a consistent subject identity across diverse scenes-remains a challenge for text-to-image (T2I) models. Existing training-free SCG methods often achieve consistency at the cost of layout and pose diversity, hindering expressive visual storytelling. To address the limitation, we propose subject-Consistent and pose-Diverse T2I framework, dubbed as CoDi, that enables consistent subject generation with diverse pose and layout. Motivated by the progressive nature of diffusion, where coarse structures emerge early and fine details are refined later, CoDi adopts a two-stage strategy: Identity Transport (IT) and Identity Refinement (IR). IT operates in the early denoising steps, using optimal transport to transfer identity features to each target image in a pose-aware manner. This promotes subject consistency while preserving pose diversity. IR is applied in the later denoising steps, selecting the most salient identity features to further refine subject details. Extensive qualitative and quantitative results on subject consistency, pose diversity, and prompt fidelity demonstrate that CoDi achieves both better visual perception and stronger performance across all metrics. The code is provided in https://github.com/NJU-PCALab/CoDi.
